A.title: The Gate of Connectives
A.prompt: Evaluate (p ∨ ¬q) ∧ r for p=T, q=F, r=T.

B.title: The Equivalence Hall
B.prompt: Are p → q and ¬p ∨ q logically equivalent?

C.title: The Chamber of Validity
C.prompt: Given: p ∨ q, ¬p ⟹ q. Is the argument valid?

D.title: Truth Table Trial
D.prompt: For p=T, q=F, what is p ↔ ¬q?

BOSS.title: 👹 Final Boss – Multi-Step Logic Trial
BOSS.prompt:
Evaluate all:
1) ¬(p ∧ q)
2) (p → r)
3) (q ∨ ¬r)
For p=F, q=T, r=F → Which option is correct?

H1.title: Hard Mode – Implication Gate
H1.prompt: Evaluate ¬(p → q) ∧ r for p=T, q=T, r=F.

H4.title: Hard Mode – Logical Trap
H4.prompt: For p=F, q=F, r=T → what is ((p ∨ q) ∧ ¬r) → p?

BOSS_H.title: 👹 Hard Mode Boss – Ultimate Logic Challenge
BOSS_H.prompt:
Given p=T, q=F, r=T: which is correct?
1) (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ (q → r)
2) ¬(p ↔ r)
3) (p ∨ q) ∧ (¬p → r)
Pick the correct overall truth values:
